q: Vectors can be multiplied in two different ways: the scalar product and the vector product.
e: True. Vectors can be multiplied in two different ways: the scalar product and the vector product. The two products are the scalar product and the vector product.

q: Vectors can be multiplied in three different ways: the scalar product, the vector product, and the tensor product.
e: False. Vectors can be multiplied in two different ways: the scalar product and the vector product. Vectors are multiplied in two ways here: the scalar (dot) product and the vector (cross) product. There is no third product in this chapter.

q: In the scalar product, a scalar can be formed by multiplying two vectors.
e: True. In the scalar product, a scalar can be formed by multiplying two vectors. Dot two vectors and you get a scalar.

q: In the scalar product, a vector can be formed by multiplying two vectors.
e: False. The claim puts vector where scalar belongs. In the scalar product, a scalar can be formed by multiplying two vectors. The scalar product outputs a number, not a vector.

q: The scalar product of vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ is defined as $\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B} = AB \cos \theta$.
e: True. The scalar product of vectors A and B is defined as A · B = AB cos θ. A · B = AB cos θ. That number is the dot product, also called the scalar product.

q: The scalar product of vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ is defined as $\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B} = AB \sin \theta$.
e: False. The claim puts sin where cos belongs. The scalar product of vectors A and B is defined as A · B = AB cos θ. The scalar product uses cos θ, not sin θ.

q: In the equation $\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B} = AB \cos \theta$, $\theta$ is the angle between $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$.
e: True. In the equation A · B = AB cos θ, θ is the angle between A and B. Keep the symbols and the sign in that relation.

q: The scalar product is also called the dot product.
e: True. The scalar product is also called the dot product. A · B = AB cos θ. That number is the dot product, also called the scalar product.

q: The scalar product is also called the cross product.
e: False. The claim puts cross where dot belongs. The scalar product is also called the dot product. A × B is the cross product, a vector perpendicular to both A and B.

q: Work is the scalar product of force and displacement.
e: True. Work is the scalar product of force and displacement. W = F · s = Fs cos θ. That is a scalar product.

q: Work is the vector product of force and displacement.
e: False. The claim puts vector where scalar belongs. Work is the scalar product of force and displacement. Work is a scalar product, F · s, not a vector product.

q: The scalar product has the commutative property as described by $\vec{A} \cdot \vec{B} = \vec{B} \cdot \vec{A}$.
e: True. The scalar product has the commutative property as described by A · B = B · A. Dot products make scalars with cos θ. Cross products make perpendicular vectors with sin θ.

q: The vector product of vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ is defined as $\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \vec{C}$.
e: True. The vector product of vectors A and B is defined as A × B = C. The vector product is A × B = C, with C = AB sin θ and C perpendicular to the A-B plane.

q: The magnitude of $\vec{C}$ in the vector product $\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \vec{C}$ is $C = AB \cos \theta$.
e: False. The cross product uses sin θ, not cos θ.

q: The direction of $\vec{C}$ in a vector product is determined by using the right-hand rule.
e: True. The direction of C in a vector product is determined by using the right-hand rule. Point fingers along A, curl them toward B, and the thumb gives A × B.

q: The direction of $\vec{C}$ is parallel to the plane that contains $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$.
e: False. A × B stands perpendicular to the plane of A and B. Parallel would be wrong.

q: The result of the vector product is a vector quantity.
e: True. The result of the vector product is a vector quantity. Dot products make scalars with cos θ. Cross products make perpendicular vectors with sin θ.

q: The vector product between two vectors is denoted by a cross ($\times$), hence this product is called the cross product.
e: True. The vector product between two vectors is denoted by a cross (×), hence this product is called the cross product. A × B is the cross product, a vector perpendicular to both A and B.

q: The vector product obeys the commutative property as $\vec{A} \times \vec{B} = \vec{B} \times \vec{A}$.
e: False. The scalar product has the commutative property as described by A · B = B · A. Dot products make scalars with cos θ. Cross products make perpendicular vectors with sin θ.

q: The formulae for the torque and the angular velocity are determined by using the vector product.
e: True. The formulae for the torque and the angular velocity are determined by using the vector product. Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt.

q: To use the right-hand rule, first you have to hold up your right hand so that index finger and middle finger are perpendicular to thumb.
e: True. To use the right-hand rule, first you have to hold up your right hand so that index finger and middle finger are perpendicular to thumb. Point fingers along A, curl them toward B, and the thumb gives A × B.

q: In the right-hand rule, your index finger points in the direction of $\vec{B}$ and your middle finger points in the direction of $\vec{A}$.
e: False. Point fingers along A, curl them toward B, and the thumb gives A × B.

q: In the right-hand rule, your thumb will point in the direction of the cross product $\vec{A} \times \vec{B}$.
e: True. In the right-hand rule, your thumb will point in the direction of the cross product A × B. A × B is the cross product, a vector perpendicular to both A and B.
